transcript:
[00:00:09.560] - Gordon
Hello.

[00:00:09.850] - Taylor
Hello.

[00:00:10.190] - Gordon
My name's Gordon from Drayson Design.

[00:00:12.010] - Taylor
And I'm Taylor from the Creative Tinker.

[00:00:14.020] - Gordon
And welcome to "This Week With Taylor and Gordon," a weekly podcast and vidcast where we talk about things that have affected our businesses over the last seven days. And welcome back to this episode 127.

[00:00:27.770] - Taylor
That's quite a lot.

[00:00:29.060] - Gordon
I'll be honest, I didn't expect to get into triple figures. I was dubious we were going to get into double figures, to be honest. But yeah here we are, 127. We are over a quarter of the way to the next hundred.

[00:00:43.430] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:00:43.890] - Gordon
It's amazing. So welcome back to those who've been with us before, and welcome to those who've never been with us before. And we have a couple of interesting topics to talk about today. First of all, any news?

[00:00:58.170] - Taylor
No, none from me.

[00:00:59.290] - Gordon
Okay, no news from me either. Let's get straight into it. Would you like to start?

[00:01:04.040] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:01:04.930] - Gordon
Okay.

[00:01:05.640] - Taylor
So a while ago when I was using Spotify, I created an integration on my website which essentially showed what I was currently listening to and it pulled live data from Spotify through Last FM which basically made it easier to be able to poll for data for the current song. I would show it on my website and then if I wasn't playing anything, it would say, 'not listening to anything.' And this would update. If I changed the song and you were still on my website, it would actually update in real time, which is quite nice. And I've been doing some mentoring recently and one of the features that they wanted to do on personalized mentoring is they wanted to add Spotify integration. So the client had a car type website and we're thinking that we can add this Spotify "currently playing in the office." The idea of the mentoring is to show him how to go about certain solutions in a more developer focused way. He's a really good designer. He's Pedro, who I built Oxi Change Log with, and I've done lots of cool projects with him. We were creating a Spotify integration, and I'd already created this on my personal site, so it was just a matter of pulling out the bits that I needed, but obviously adapting it to work the way that they wanted, or he wanted, sorry. Because his setup is slightly different to how I had it and mine was in a block form, so it was reusable; so there's things there that weren't needed and things like that. We had a good time breaking it down, working through it, why certain things were there. Hit a few snags, but we got them fixed. And yeah, he signed up for a Last FM or connected the Spotify account to Last FM. And yeah, now if you visit their website, although it's currently still being built, but if you were to visit their website, it would show if they were listening to something on Spotify. And if not, it would say 'not listening to anything.'

[00:03:22.150] - Gordon
So that's really interesting because you don't use Spotify currently, do you?

[00:03:26.360] - Taylor
No. So I switched to Apple Music. So yeah, my Spotify integration is just on my site, but I don't use it because Apple don't have any API like that that you can easily pull from without draining your battery, essentially. And I already drain my battery enough with my other automations.

[00:03:48.020] - Gordon
And the fact that you're running the beta software currently with iOS 17. So that's testing software. So that could very easily be draining your battery as well.

[00:03:59.550] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:03:59.930] - Gordon
Look how much taller I am than you today. Oh, okay. You're not wearing your thing on your neck, are you, to make sure you're standing up properly?

[00:04:09.440] - Taylor
No.

[00:04:09.880] - Gordon
That's what it is. Okay, so the Spotify integration is all done and it's working?

[00:04:15.030] - Taylor
Yeah, it was working well. The only thing was it wasn't updating live if you changed the song. And I'm not sure why that was. So next session, we're going to look into that and see if we can fix it. And we also fixed some of the Fluent Form issues. They recently released a massive 5.0 update, which came with a lot of new things, new UI, new features, a REST API. One of the things that they did is they deprecated a lot of the hooks, the filter hooks, which they would still work, but you basically would get a warning to say, "Please use the new hooks." Essentially, they're all the same, apart from its Fluent Forms slash your hook name, rather than Fluent Form underscore your hook name. So we fixed that as well, which was good.

[00:05:06.140] - Gordon
And Fluent Forms has had several minor updates since with little bugs that come out when you have a major version. So I think it's 5.0:3 is the latest. So 5.0:1, 5.0:2, 5.0:3, which means that I've been doing an awful lot of updating on an awful lot of sites. And in fact, I had an issue with one of my forms where a button that we'd specified to be a certain size in a column, the column size was a certain size, so that the text was on one line, changed and broke. And it changed it to a smaller size. So it was on two lines, which wasn't great. And there may be other issues that I haven't found yet. But one of these things when you do have an update that come out like this is to go and test the functionality of that plug-in just to make sure that it's working as expected because the last thing you want, especially with a form plug-in, is for it not to be sending forms to you. So it's a really good idea to get them tested.

[00:06:10.410] - Taylor
Yeah, definitely.

[00:06:12.080] - Gordon
Anything else you have to say on your subject?

[00:06:14.400] - Taylor
No, I don't think so. Just having fun with APIs and reusing codes that I'd written two years ago now and refactoring it as I went because there's always ways you can refactor it, write it better, things like that.

[00:06:29.060] - Gordon
Well, that's right. New ways of doing things, new APIs, new knowledge, lots of different reasons to refactor code. So I'd like to talk about V1CE cards. Now, it's spelt V1CE, so it's not as you would expect it to be. But these cards are rather nifty. They're rather clever. So they're like credit cards. So you can get them in different materials. We'll come back to that. But we've chosen, or I've chosen, and you're getting for your birthday, a plastic one. Now, the plastic card looks just like a credit card. Same thickness as far as I understand. It hasn't arrived yet. But you can have it printed on one side with whatever design you want. That could be your name, it could be your logo, it could be anything you like, really. And depending on the material that you use will depend on how it gets printed. And on the other side is a QR code. So let me go through the functionality of it first, and then we'll go back to the materials and things that you can choose. So it, first of all, has a QR code on it so that anybody can scan the QR code. Come back to what that does in a second. The second functionality is an NFC chip inside it. So you can tap on a device that has NFC, like a mobile phone, for example, and it will do your recommended action. Now, there is an app that goes with these cards and what you can do is you can set up different profiles. Now, a profile could be a packet of information. So it could be a website address, simple as that. It could be a contact card which has your name, your address, your telephone numbers, your social media, etc. All of that in one go. It could be that it's a deep link. So for example, if you've got a Facebook page, it could be a link that will load when they scan the QR code or they get the tap, it will take them into the Facebook app and take them to your Facebook page, but in the app rather than as a URL. And there are lots of other different things you can have. So you could have a lead capture, where you can have a form that is submitted on their phone, on the person who's being tapped on's phone, and they just fill it in. And then that sends all the information back to you so that you can then add them as a contact or a lead. And it's a really interesting way of doing things because you can change the profile that you're sending on that QR code or the NFC chip every single time it gets used. So if you've got more than one business, as I do, I can set up multiple profiles. And if I turn up and see someone and want to give them my details, I just choose the one that I want on my phone, and then I can use the card just tap, and all the correct information will go to that person. And I can just change it as many times as I like. Now, I don't know if there's a limit to the number of profiles you can have. I'm pretty sure there is, but I don't know what that is. There is no limit to the number of taps that you can have, or scans of your QR code, once you have the actual card. And it's a really clever software. It's basically the software that's doing all the work because that QR code is sending them different information every time that they scan it, depending on what you want them to receive. But it's a really nice solution to save having to give out business cards or having business cards on you all the time.

[00:10:29.010] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:10:29.430] - Gordon
And if you don't have your business card on you or your V1CE card, you can also, I believe, add it to your Apple Wallet so that you've got the QR code there that you can then allow people to just scan from your phone directly. And I think you can do the QR code from within the app as well. So you don't have to have that card with you, which is really cool. Now, the price of these depends on the material that you use. So the one that we've gone for is the plastic one. I thought it would be the most durable, and that works out at 40 pounds for the card. And you can send them a full colour CMYK print so that they'll print one side of it completely. In fact, your one is edge to edge print.

[00:11:22.020] - Taylor
Yes.

[00:11:22.400] - Gordon
So it's completely covered and it looks just like your business card, which is great. I've just got my logo on it. You can choose different colour bases for the plastic ones. You're going to have a blue or a yellow. In our case, we got white and silver. So that's the first. You can have matt and gloss as well. I think we both went for gloss.

[00:11:42.200] - Taylor
Yes.

[00:11:42.360] - Gordon
So it gives a better print. The other materials that they have are bamboo, which is an unusual one. So bamboo is actually the wood bamboo, and it absorbs the ink more. So you can print on it with the grain showing. The problem with bamboo, in my opinion, is it's susceptible to water and it can warp and so on. So I didn't particularly want that. Even though bamboo is sustainable and I can understand why people would want to use that. The next step up from that is metal. And you can choose a couple of different types of metal. And instead of it printing on the metal, it etches out of the metal. So it's like one, it's like a duotone? Yeah, so you've got a tint, effectively, because it's gouging out part of the metal to give a different colour, effectively. So that's the way you do that. And then they're top... I think that's about £100. And then their top card is 24 carat gold.

[00:12:56.290] - Taylor
You didn't get that one for me?

[00:12:57.380] - Gordon
No, I didn't. Why would you want a 24 carat gold card? I'd be worried about taking it out with me. 24 carat gold card. And again, that's etched. So I'm guessing laser etched. So it's taking the material away. So you've got the two tone for that as well. And that I think was £300, something like that. But we've ordered them. We've sent them our artwork. Quite often the designers will just receive a logo and they will then do whatever you want. You tell them where you want the logo to go and they'll do it, send you a proof. Because we sent full artwork, they sent us the proof and we checked it earlier this week. And it should take 2-3 days to print and get to us.

[00:13:49.110] - Taylor
Okay.

[00:13:49.640] - Gordon
So when they arrive, we'll tell you what we think. I think it's quite an interesting concept. We'll put a link in the show notes. If they do affiliate links, we'll have an affiliate link there. If not, it'll just be a regular link. If it is an affiliate link, it means that there's something that we get from it for recommending them. Now, I can't recommend them fully because I haven't actually received the product yet. But so far, everything is good. I like the process. I like the app. We've got to play with the app. And linking the app to your account is really easy. You just have the app on your phone which is already logged in. You take the card that arrives in the post, you tap it on your phone, and you're then linked, which is really quick and easy, I think.

[00:14:38.650] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:14:39.030] - Gordon
But I like the idea of having one business card that you have with you that you can then give to multiple people multiple times. Now, you've actually got something coming from Kickstarter that is similar to this, isn't it?

[00:14:54.530] - Taylor
Yes. So I backed the AirCard, which a while ago I spoke about the Edge Pros, which I backed by Rolling Square, I believe. They're a Swedish company, I believe. And they've Kickstarted quite a lot of products. I've backed three products of theirs now. They have come up with something called an AirCard. And what it is is it uses the same technology that your air tags use and it allows you to use it as a 'find my...' AirCard. So you can put this in your wallet so you can then find the AirCard. You can track it on the same app that you would use for your phone, for your devices, for your air tags, and you're also able to see your wallet. Which because it's slightly different in terms of a wallet is normally flat, it basically acts like another card, which is quite nice.

[00:15:54.220] - Gordon
An air tag would be difficult to put in a wallet because it's bulbous, isn't it? So it's not flat like a card is, whereas this is. Like a credit card.

[00:16:04.580] - Taylor
And then they've also added the ability to have a link, NFC type thing that you can do. Similar thing to what the V1CE card can do, but not as complex because that's not the main feature of it. The main feature is the find my.

[00:16:20.030] - Gordon
Yeah. And so what I think I'm going to do is I'm going to put them both together because this is actually a Father's Day present to me.

[00:16:25.640] - Taylor
Yes.

[00:16:26.040] - Gordon
The Aircard, which is really nice. We give each other tech that we think we'd enjoy and they'd enjoy for birthdays and presents and things, which is quite nice. So I think what I'm going to do is, because I've got an RFID wallet coming, which is going to be able to hold a certain number of cards. So I think what I might do is put my AirCard and my V1CE card into it, so that I'll be able to find my V1CE card when I can't find it and the AirCard will be allowing me to find it. And then I've also got pretty much everything I need to be able to tap onto different people and let them have my details. So yeah, that's not due until September, I think. Something around there. August time maybe, around that time. So when that arrives, we'll tell you about that as well. So that's everything from me. We'll put links for these things in the show notes.

[00:17:20.710] - Taylor
That's everything from me as well.

[00:17:22.190] - Gordon
Thank you for joining us. As always, you can like, share, and subscribe. Our videos can be found on YouTube and on Facebook.

[00:17:30.250] - Taylor
You can also go to our website thisweekwith.co.uk to find all of our past episodes.

[00:17:35.430] - Gordon
And of course, subscribe on your favourite podcast app so that you can just listen to us in the car. Until next week, 1pm on Friday. We'll see you then. My name is Gordon and I'm from Drayson Design.

[00:17:49.550] - Taylor
And I'm Taylor from The Creative Tinker.

[00:17:52.020] - Gordon
Goodbye.

[00:17:52.720] - Taylor
Bye.

transcript:
[00:00:09.220] - Gordon
Hello.

[00:00:09.500] - Taylor
Hello.

[00:00:09.820] - Gordon
My name's Gordon from Drayson Design.

[00:00:11.570] - Taylor
And I'm Taylor from The Creative Tinker.

[00:00:13.450] - Gordon
And welcome to "This Week with Taylor and Gordon," a weekly podcast and vidcast where we talk about things that have affected our businesses over the last seven days. And how's your last seven days been?

[00:00:25.120] - Taylor
It's been good.

[00:00:26.680] - Gordon
Excellent. I've been rebuilding my computer systems again.

[00:00:34.280] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:00:34.860] - Gordon
Just getting them all back up and running. And in fact, that's what I'd like to talk about today. Can I start?

[00:00:40.010] - Taylor
Go for it.

[00:00:41.120] - Gordon
So what I do when I have new equipment; I bought a brand new computer, I bought a brand new monitor. So this is going to replace my main machine. So what happens to my main machine? Well, the previous main machine gets moved down the line. So I have two computers in my office for many reasons. One is originally that it was used by other people, and more commonly now, it's used for tasks that I don't want to bog my main machine down in. So things like capturing video from tapes, for example, that's one of the things it does. And it also manages all of the scans that we do that go up to Evernote, which I'll talk about again, because I don't think I've spoken about that for a long time, and it's worth coming back to in a future episode. So it gets tasks that are given to it, and it goes and does it, and it doesn't bog down my main machine. So what happens is, when my main machine gets replaced, the machine that was there gets moved down the line. Now, that's not quite as simple as it sounds, because what you have to do is you have to migrate all the data from your current new machine to the new, new machine so that all the data gets sent across. Now, I quite like reinstalling applications because sometimes you end up with a lot of rubbish in the library files, and you end up with parts of programs that you've tried and used, or you don't use anymore and you've taken off the system. And so it's much nicer to have a machine that's got just the data, all the files, and then reinstall the applications. That's the ideal way of doing it. So you do that, and then you use the new machine. But sometimes settings don't come across, or profile files, or little config files, these things that you're used to. And you start using the programs on the new machine and you go, "Oh, no wait, I've lost all of my settings for Photoshop," or "I've lost all this, I've lost all my actions," whatever it is. So I always have my older machine, so what used to be the current machine, to the side of me, and that's powered up. And so whenever I get to that situation, I can either go and look and I can just put the settings in, or I can export a file and move it across, and I have it there for...

[00:03:26.340] - Computer
Time for a five minute break.

[00:03:27.930] - Gordon
Made me jump that did. That's Taylor's computer telling him to have a five minute break, which means that he has to move and stretch. So everybody, here we go, five minute break. Not a five minute break, but just have a stretch. There we go. So yes, I leave it there, and I leave it there for maybe a week or two because it's really important that I don't get rid of what's on that machine until I know I've got everything. Now, normally, not on this occasion, normally, I have an up to date backup of it on time machine, which means if I do mess up, I can at least go back to the time machine and get the files that I need. But it's been a couple of weeks now since I've had my new machine. So the machine that used to be my main machine, I'm pretty confident I've got most of what I need from it. So this machine is now being reformatted. It's having a new operating system put on. So it's as if it was a brand new machine out of the box. It then gets moved down the line. So the machine that was my secondary machine now is going to be moved on. And my old main machine now becomes my secondary machine. So the way I do that is I migrate all the data onto what used to be the main machine, check it's all working, make sure everything's done. And again, that takes another week or two just to make sure I've got everything. So it's about a month for me to move a machine down the line. But the way I do it means that hopefully I don't miss anything. So I'm actually using my new machines in day to day activities just to see if there's anything that I'm missing, at least I have the opportunity to get it back before I repurpose the machine. This then leaves what used to be my secondary machine as a spare machine. So what do I do with that? Well, normally, once it's got everything off it and I'm happy that I've got everything, that machine gets reformatted, it gets a new operating system put on it, and then I sell it.

[00:05:39.450] - Taylor
Nice.

[00:05:39.920] - Gordon
So I get a little bit of money back that goes towards the purchase of my new machine that I'm now using as my main machine. It's not normally a lot of money, but it's something that I do because the machines that I use are still good machines. They might be probably about six or seven years old by the time it stops being a secondary machine. And so it's an older machine, but it's still good enough for those people who want to just browse the internet and do emails. That's fine. It's good enough... I mean, it's been capturing video on Final Cut Pro, so it's good enough for video capture and editing. Might be a little bit slow for editing some of the newer formats. I wouldn't expect to be able to do 4K on it, for example. But it's still got life in it. And there are people who want to have a Mac, an iMac in particular, and they just can't afford a new Mac, or they just don't want one of the new Macs, and they want one of the older ones because they prefer them. So there is a market out there for that. So it's going to be put on the market. So if you're looking for an older iMac, then I will post on our This Week With Facebook group a link to where it's being sold, and you can go and buy it. And the nice thing is that I do like to keep the original boxes for things. So I do have the original box for it, so it will be packaged up properly and I'll make sure that it's got the operating system on and it's all ready to go, basically. So if you've got equipment that you're moving down the line, always look to see what you can do with the machines at the end of the line and see if there's anything you can do to maybe give it away, sell it, give it to friends or family, give it another life. Don't just throw it in landfill because they normally have a bit of life left in them and someone is going to be appreciative of that. Talking of new machines, I've just bought some new headphones.

[00:07:54.190] - Taylor
Oh, yeah?

[00:07:54.640] - Gordon
Yeah, I bought some new Bose Quiet Comfort 45s, which is the model number. I had the 25s. You bought the 35s. And then 45s came out, and that's what I've just bought. And the only reason I did that is because of Camel Camel. And it's worth mentioning that here. Camel Camel is a website that will track prices of Amazon products. So all you do is you put the URL in and you tell it what price you're looking for, and it will email you if the price ever comes down to that price.

[00:08:27.480] - Taylor
That's very clever.

[00:08:27.810] - Gordon
And so normally, these headphones are £319 for the Quiet Comfort 45s, but I have seen them on sale for £249 in the past. So I put my target as £245, and I got an email just yesterday, in fact, and it came through. £189! Which is well below my target.

[00:08:50.560] - Taylor
That's very good.

[00:08:50.850] - Gordon
And it's such a good price I ordered them there and then, and they arrived today. So I've got new headphones. So it might be that I'll put my Quiet Comfort 25s online as well. They need new ear cups, which you can get third party ones for because they're splitting a bit. But apart from that, they're perfectly fine and they're very very good. They've got noise cancelling in them. So there you go, something else that I'll try and put on the Facebook group. That's it. What are you going to talk about?

[00:09:16.870] - Taylor
So this week I was refactoring some codes, so I did some custom work for another agency, for their client, and it was to do with Fluent Forms. And their client came back, probably about six months later, and said they wanted a change; because of the way the market was they wanted to add more brands of boilers. So it was a boiler quote form thing. And they wanted to add more brands of boilers. And the current system, or the way that I'd built it didn't allow for that. So they said, "Is it possible to update it so that it can accept different brands?"

[00:09:57.560] - Gordon
And allow the customer to put those brands in?

[00:10:00.640] - Taylor
Yeah, exactly. And so the way that I'd built it didn't allow for it exactly. But because of the way that I'd built it, it didn't take too much to extend it and add that functionality, which is quite nice. And while I was at it, I refactored my code so that it was a bit better. One of the things was changing from using an Ajax function to using a "REST API" and then using "Fetch," which is a much better way of handling data from the front end to the back end, and sending that back to the front end. So yeah, it was a bit of refactoring. It's horrible looking at my previous code because you obviously get better as time goes on. So looking at my old code, I thought, "Wow, I didn't write this very well." So I refactored a bit of it. And then also, I have been working on a new snippet for Snippet Club. So one of Kyle's clients is Yoast. He was the founder of "Yoast SEO." And on his blog, he has an 'Upcoming Gigs' section. And it's a two by two grid with the first item being a call to action where it says, "Would you like me to speak at your event? Get in contact." And then it has the next three upcoming gigs that he has. Now, this is all static. It was created, you just have to manually update it when they become old. And I thought what would be a nice way would be creating a post type and using posts to do it. And you could obviously set a date so that when it's in the past, it automatically updates to show the next upcoming gig. But the hardest part was inserting static content into essentially a dynamic loop. And I managed to find a solution or create a solution that would allow you to hook in using the Generate Press hooks, which is one of the biggest and really nice functionalities of Generate Press. And you can essentially hook in either before or after the query loop. So this is really useful to be able to add content at the beginning or the end, like a call to action, or say you don't have enough posts, so you only have an odd number, you could insert a static thing just to make it even. And it was a really nice solution that can be used in a lot of different ways. I'm currently exploring how we could use similar code to insert ads throughout your loop. Apple support is the best - you can ring them any time during your ownership of their product 1Password - Password Manager - https://1password.com/ Mange all your passwords and sensitive information Master password unlocks all the others Classic version which was licensed, is slowly going away - cloud and subscription based is the future Gordon was upset having to pay a subscription, however 1Password offered 50% discount on the first three years All data is encrypted Unlimited devices - data is all in 1Passwords cloud Credit and Debit cards can also be added - along with bank details API available Knows what website you are on, or application you have loaded and offers passwords for them Watchtower feature monitors duplicate, and leaked passwords so you can keep them secure Unlimited vaults - so you can share passwords and data with other members of the family The safest way to create passwords is to make sure they are all random letters, numbers and symbols, and different for every single use Offers to update existing and save new logins Not sponsored by 1Password - we are just happy users Google are looking to eradicate passwords completely - https://blog.google/technology/safety-security/one-step-closer-to-a-passwordless-future/ Command line available for developers   Visit the website: https://www.thisweekwith.co.uk Drayson Design Website - https://www.draysondesign.com The Creative Tinker Website - https://www.thecreativetinker.com Facebook: https://www.thisweekwith.co.uk/facebook Youtube: https://www.thisweekwith.co.uk/youtube * Full transcript will be available on the website. transcript:
[00:00:09.100] - Gordon
Hello. My name's Gordon from Drayson Design.

[00:00:11.610] - Taylor
And I'm Taylor from The Creative Tinker.

[00:00:13.890] - Gordon
And welcome to "This Week with Taylor and Gordon," a weekly podcast and vidcast where we talk about things that have affected our businesses over the last seven days. And thank you so much for joining us. So it's been a stressful week for me.

[00:00:28.890] - Taylor
Yeah?

[00:00:29.290] - Gordon
Yeah. So not only do I have problems with my hard drives, as I was saying last week, but I also had my computer which needed an interim update, which I did, and it restarted so that it could start up with the new update and it wouldn't restart.

[00:00:48.330] - Taylor
Not good.

[00:00:49.450] - Gordon
Not good at all. So yeah. The good thing is Apple support, their telephone support is really good. I gave them a call and they talked through various options with me. And the one I went with was to back up the hard drive onto a separate hard drive, wipe the computer, and then reinstall from time machine, which took about three days.

[00:01:14.910] - Taylor
Wow!

[00:01:14.910] - Gordon
Which was quite a long time, but I am now back up and running. So thank goodness for that. But have you ever tried Apple Support?

[00:01:23.580] - Taylor
I have. Yeah, I have a couple of times.

[00:01:26.910] - Gordon
What's really good is they don't limit you to the warranty period. So quite often you'll get 12 months worth of support and then that's it. With Apple, you can ring them up about a five year old machine and they'll help you.

[00:01:40.000] - Taylor
Yeah, that's really good.

[00:01:40.000] - Gordon
They're really good at that. So hopefully whatever system you have, you'll be able to get just as good support. But I'll be honest, I'm not sure it's going to be as good as Apple's. Apple is very good. So what are we going to talk about this week, Taylor?

[00:01:57.800] - Taylor
We are going to talk about 1Password.

[00:02:00.840] - Gordon
Okay. So 1Password is an application that I've been using now for about 15 years, I think, something like that. The idea behind it is it's an application where you have all of your logins, all of your passwords from anywhere, whether that be on the internet or whether it be in real life. You can have...

[00:02:24.880] - Taylor
All your sensitive and secure information.

[00:02:26.530] - Gordon
Sensitive information. You can have pin codes for alarms, anything that's not online, but mainly for websites and for accounts and all this sort of thing. And it's called 1Password because it stores all of your passwords and your data behind a one password. So you have a master password that unlocks the application and then gives you access to all the other passwords. And it's been really really good. I recommended it to you. You've used it for a long time. Problem is that the Safari browser has a little... What's it called? An extension that allows you to input your login details to a website by going to the website and then it'll auto fill it for you. And the classic version, which is what I've always had, has been a license key that you buy for a version. So we had a 1Password 7, which was the version that I paid my license for. I paid lots of other licenses; I think I started it when it was 1Password 3, something like that. So every time there's been a new license, I've updated. However, they went cloud based and because of that, they decided not to update the Safari browser extension any further than July the first. So July the first, we were going to lose access to all of our browser access, basically. In fact, I think they were keeping Safari, but in the future, it's likely to die at some point. And they've gone cloud based, which I get. Most companies who want to stick around.

[00:04:28.990] - Taylor
Well, cloud and subscription based.

[00:04:30.280] - Gordon
Yeah, cloud based and subscription based. And I get it. I understand why they do that. I do subscription based services as well, and it helps to bring money in so that you can then continue to grow and build the service. But for those people who already had the classic, which was basically a one-off license fee, it's a bit of a kick in the teeth, really. So I was not happy. So I emailed them, and I said to them, "Is there any other option? Because I don't really want to pay annually for what I'm getting for free at the moment." And they came back and they said, "Yeah, the next version up, version 8 is very good. It allows you to do all sorts of things you can't do at the moment. And I'll tell you what, we'll give you 50% discount on the next three annual subscriptions."

[00:05:30.410] - Taylor
That's good.

[00:05:31.570] - Gordon
Yeah. So I had a look and it was like $60 per year. So that would have worked out at $30 a year. And that's for a family subscription, which gives you up to five members of your family. And you know what? I do use it. And if they've gone subscription based, it means that they're not going to be doing licences anymore. And it means that I get the latest updates. And it's a little bit like paying for a license now, but every year you're getting the updates.

[00:06:05.930] - Taylor
It's also, I think it's one of those things that you probably don't want to skimp out on in terms of... It's where all pretty much your entire life is stored in terms of the security. And there's been a lot of data breaches and multiple data breaches for some companies within the space of a couple of months. And you think, "Well, you're paying for the security and they're having data breaches." And I think 1Password is probably one of the best password managers out there that have very limited data breaches. And I can't remember the last time they've had a data breach.

[00:06:42.360] - Gordon
I don't believe they have. And the other thing is that all the data is encrypted anyway. And when you actually sign up for the cloud service, you get sent a secret key, which you need if you forget your login details. If you don't have that secret key, you don't get back in because even 1Password can't access it because it's all encrypted.

[00:07:04.860] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:07:04.860] - Gordon
Which means if there was a data breach, they're not going to take very much because they can't, it's all encrypted. So yeah, I mean I use this service a lot and I don't begrudge spending the money. I have supported them in the past with all the license updates every time they bring out a new version. But it is a great bit of software. Do you want to explain what you can do with the new version, maybe, that you couldn't do with the old version?

[00:07:34.670] - Taylor
So the new version has things like copying universal clipboard, so you can copy between, you know copy on your computer and paste it on your iPhone or something like that?

[00:07:44.850] - Gordon
Yeah, I should say you get access to the app on all devices. So you change your password on one website, it goes into 1Password, it's then available on all your other devices. You can even log in as a web user. But I think you need your secret key to do that. So you have to have that available to you.

[00:08:06.110] - Taylor
Yeah. So you've obviously got your global password that updates for everything. They have QR codes now, so you can scan a QR code. I'm not sure what it does.

[00:08:15.450] - Gordon
It adds a new device. So it basically allows you to download the app onto your phone, for example, scan the QR code, and it'll say, "Right, this is your account. This has been verified. We're going to set you up with this account as if you'd logged in now," which is great.

[00:08:31.870] - Taylor
They have different types of vaults and things like that. Again, you can have better access and you can create vaults and share access a lot easier. So the way we were doing it before, we had to use Dropbox, which again, probably isn't the secureist because it's stored on Dropbox. So then you've got another thing to worry about. If you've got a data breach on Dropbox, then that's where all of your things are stored and they're probably not as encrypted. Obviously, the file itself is encrypted, but they probably don't have the same level of encryption for the actual entire server that 1Password probably have.

[00:09:08.510] - Gordon
And interestingly, I have a free account on Dropbox. I don't pay for it. And so I am limited to three devices. So I could only have 1Password on three devices with Dropbox storing my vault. Whereas now, I have unlimited devices. I can put them on as many as I need to.

[00:09:29.520] - Taylor
What other features are there?

[00:09:31.680] - Gordon
I should say without 1Password, I probably would not be able to get into 95% of the websites that I have logins for.

[00:09:43.460] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:09:44.660] - Gordon
I don't know what the passwords are because they're generated, they're random, they're letters and numbers, and upper case, lower case, symbols. I have no idea what they are.

[00:09:56.000] - Taylor
So you do have the browser based keychains. So Safari has their own, Firefox has their own, Chrome, Brave, whatever, all have their own, but they don't always sync. And if you do want them to sync, you have to be using the exact same browser across every single device. So I don't use Safari on my computer, but I use it on my phone. And so all of my stuff gets stored in the Firefox in the keychain on my computer, but gets stored to Safari's keychain on my phone. And so I would never be able to keep everything in sync, whereas 1Password works, regardless of the browser. And you can have the browser extension on all your devices and all your browser extensions.

[00:10:33.500] - Gordon
It also allows you to store credit card and debit card and bank details. Again, it's all encrypted so that should you need them, you know you're out and about, you don't have your credit card on you, you can log into 1Password and just use all the details. You can put everything in there. It's all encrypted hidden behind this security, so it's very safe to use it.

[00:10:57.770] - Taylor
They've got a quick access little pop up menu so you can quickly search all of your passwords. So I had an Alfred snippet that did basically similar to this. You would type 1P space, and then what you wanted to search for, and it would return all your passwords, the titles of them, and you can hit Enter to open them up and see what the password is and things like that, which is quite useful because it's easy and quick to be able to search your entire password database.

[00:11:28.750] - Gordon
And now it's all built in.

[00:11:30.450] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:11:31.210] - Gordon
The other thing that it does is it's very smart. So it knows what website you're on. It also knows what application you've loaded, and it will offer suggestions. "Is this what you want me to fill?" And you can click Auto fill. It'll automatically put the details in the right place, which is really, really useful.

[00:11:52.360] - Taylor
Another good feature is the watch tower. So this is, it scans for data breaches. So if there's been a data breach, it will say there has been a data breach for this website or whatever. And then it also scans for your weak passwords. So if you were reused before, it would say you've reused a certain password a hundred times or whatever. Or it will say it's just a weak password in general. And then you get a score. And obviously, the higher the score, the better. And you can obviously make changes to make sure that all of your passwords are up to date and they're all secure. You haven't reused them. And also if there's been a data breach, you've updated and changed it since.

[00:12:35.960] - Gordon
Yeah, and it's really useful. It tells you about duplicates. It tells you if you've got any websites that are insecure, as in they're not using HTTPS, the S being the secure part, which is the little padlock, which is really useful. And as you said earlier, you can put all of your logins, for example, all your data, into different vaults. So for example, I have my own personal vault, which has all my own personal logins and data that only I have access to. Taylor has the same. He's got his own personal one. We then have a shared one, which is tools that we use, website services, that sort of thing, where we have one login or license keys, where we have one license key between us that we've purchased between us. And so we put that in the shared vault. And by having access to the shared vault, we both have access that we can then use and change. So if the password changes, for example, a password on a website or a license key, that can be changed in one of them and it automatically updates on all of mine as well as all of Taylor's, because it's used in the shared vault. We also have one for the family. So we have a shared family vault and in there we currently don't have very much because we've never had this before. But I put all of our passport details in there so that while we're away, if we lose our passport, at least we've got the number and all the details that we need already in our phone or our devices or accessible online. So we can get information like that back again. And if there's any other family based logins that I can put in there, like TV license, that's a family based one. And there's going to be lots of others that I can't think of at the moment. Fuel bills, fuel accounts, they can all go in the family one because that way, if someone else in the family wants to get into it or deal with it, they've got the login details, they can do so, which is great, really useful. Anything else that you can think of that's really useful on this?

[00:14:53.940] - Taylor
Erm...

[00:14:54.850] - Gordon
If you don't have a password manager, by the way, you really should. Because everyone says that you should have different passwords for every different thing that you use passwords for. And I think this is true. You should definitely do that because otherwise, if you have someone who finds out your password and you use it everywhere, they'll get into everything. And that's really, really bad for you as a person to have someone having access to all of your passwords. Plus it's a nightmare to go and change them all. If you have to go in and change all your passwords because you've lost one password and everyone now has access to it, and you've got to go in and change your password on a thousand different websites. What a nightmare. Yeah, terrible. If you lose one password and you have to go and change one website, well, that's hardly a problem, is it?

[00:15:48.450] - Taylor
Yeah, the only annoying thing is when you have things like our MetaQuest 2, which you can't have access to your 1Password. So if you were logging in on someone else's computer or somewhere where you don't have access to be able to copy and paste, it can be annoying because they're normally just random characters and letters and numbers and things.

[00:16:12.160] - Gordon
But you don't need to put them in very often that way.

[00:16:14.360] - Taylor
No, but they're still...

[00:16:15.340] - Gordon
It is still a pain.

[00:16:15.340] - Taylor
...Sometimes annoying. Especially with awkward keyboards that you get.

[00:16:19.140] - Gordon
Yeah, and things like Netflix and stuff on an Apple TV, you still have to manually put that in. And I have to go on to my 1Password and put it in character by character because I have no idea what it is because it makes no sense. It's just gobbledygook. But that's the most secure way of doing it.

[00:16:34.480] - Taylor
They do have the Apple TV remote for your phone now, so you can actually copy and paste.

[00:16:39.660] - Gordon
That is true.

[00:16:40.390] - Taylor
Which is nice. But things like MetaQuest, you just don't have control over. And when you are signing up for things on the WiFi, you've got a PlayStation or things like that, again, that used to be annoying because they didn't have a remote for you like they do for the Apple TV.

[00:16:56.200] - Gordon
And I should say, if you change your password on a website that 1Password already knows about, it will then pop up a little box saying, "you've changed the password, shall I update it for you in your records?" And you go, "yes please," and it remembers it for you.

[00:17:10.350] - Taylor
And it does the same when you're creating a new account. It recognises you've created a new account. "Do you want me to save?" And it saves all the details for you.

[00:17:18.160] - Gordon
Yeah, which is really good. And it will generate its own passwords. I think we mentioned that. But you can specify how long you want the password to be, whether you want it to have upper, lowercase letters, whether you want it to have numbers, whether you want it to have symbols. You get to choose, really. And obviously, the more of these you have set to yes, the more secure your password is going to be.

[00:17:39.750] - Taylor
There's a really good website which basically shows you, you put your password in it shows you how long it would take a computer to crack your password, which you got to be careful about because sometimes it could be dodgy putting the password in. But at the same time, it goes to show how long it would take for a six word password versus a 32 character password.

[00:18:05.990] - Gordon
Yep.

[00:18:05.990] - Taylor
And obviously, the better technology gets, the easier it becomes.

[00:18:10.480] - Gordon
Quicker it becomes, especially with AI. I'm sure there's people out there using AI to crack passwords. It wouldn't surprise me. So yeah, we've not been asked to talk about 1Password, and we've not been sponsored by them. I think I will send them a link to this so that they know that we've done it. It's always nice to tell people about the products that you're talking about. But no, we've not been sponsored at all. If they want to let us have a lifetime account, that'd be lovely. But that's not what we're going for here. We use it because we love it, and we're telling you about it because we think it's really good. If you don't have it, we'll put a link in the show notes and go and have a look. It won't be a... I don't believe they have an affiliate scheme, so it won't be an affiliate link. It will just be a link because we want you to have a secure password. And I think that's their aim. I think 1Password's aim is to make sure that everybody uses really secure passwords. Quite interestingly, I was reading an article just this week about Google who are trying to get rid of passwords. So there is a time in the future where maybe we won't need passwords and everything will be biometric. Or I'm not entirely sure. I didn't really grasp what Google were doing as far as their passwordless systems.

[00:19:45.640] - Taylor
They're normally authentication through another device, which is normally how they do it and things like that.

[00:19:51.680] - Gordon
Okay. Which is fine as long as you've got that other device with you.

[00:19:55.230] - Taylor
Yes.

[00:19:55.380] - Gordon
Or you have another device. If you're out and about and you only have your phone on you, that's not going to be helpful. So I'm guessing they've thought this through. But 1Password is quite adaptable. I'm sure that if something like this comes along, they will adapt and find a way to be able to support whatever comes in, whether that be biometric or something else. So yeah. Anything else you want to say?

[00:20:20.690] - Taylor
For the developers out there, they have a command line. So if you have SSH keys for things like GitHub, they have integrations with that. So you can basically SSH into 1Password, and you don't need to know the key. You don't need to copy and paste it. You can just use the command line to do that. Which could be useful as well.

[00:20:43.520] - Gordon
Yeah. that's really good, yeah. And I think they offer other developer opportunities as well so maybe there's something you can look at and see if there's anything that would be of interest to you. Maybe there'll be some website based 1Password stuff in the future. Who knows?

[00:21:02.350] - Taylor
Who knows?

[00:21:03.160] - Gordon
Who knows? So I think that's everything from me.

[00:21:06.070] - Taylor
And me as well.

[00:21:06.890] - Gordon
Thank you so much for joining us. As always, we can be found on Facebook and on YouTube. Please like, share, and subscribe.

[00:21:14.760] - Taylor
You can also go to our website thisweekwith.co.uk to find all of our past episodes and anything we may have spoken about.

[00:21:21.030] - Gordon
We should say we apologise for the delay in last week's episode. It got delayed going out. I don't know why, but we had issues and hopefully they're fixed now. We were a few hours late, I think. So apologies if you were waiting for it and it didn't come. But this one should be on time. We should be fine. I think we're okay. Yeah, I think we're okay. So please join us again next week at 1pm on Friday. Until then, my name is Gordon, I'm from Drayson Design.

[00:21:55.490] - Taylor
And I'm Taylor from The Creative Tinker.

[00:21:58.840] - Gordon
Goodbye.

[00:22:00.640] - Taylor
Bye.

We've not had a coronation here in my lifetime and definitely not in your lifetime. So yeah, very exciting. The UK do pomp and circumstance very well. So it should be a good event. We shall see.

[00:01:33.090] - Taylor

Network Access Storage.

[00:02:02.050] - Gordon
Exactly. Yeah, no it is. I got it wrong last week. So it's Network Access Storage. The system I've been using just failed on me, which was a major pain in the backside because all of the data is in a particular format and you can't just take the drives out of one box and put them into a completely new box that's made by another company because it just won't work. So that I'm effectively back where I was about a week ago. So the issue I've got is getting the data off. I need to have the drives all online in one go because otherwise, I can't access the data. I've also had to spend money out on a software that is supposed to and it hasn't quite worked yet, it's supposed to find all the data and allow me access to it so I can copy it off the drives into somewhere else and then back on the drives once they're in the new system. That's about £140 worth of software.

[00:04:42.590] - Taylor
Okay.

[00:04:43.660] - Gordon
My problem is, because it's such a large, raid system, the time it tells me it's going to take is about 257 hours.

[00:04:57.660] - Taylor
That's a long time.

[00:04:59.940] - Gordon
That's a long time. It's like 10 days, 11 days, which is a huge amount of time. And the software that I'm using is Beta because it works better with the system I've got. But it's Beta, which means that every now and then it's going to crash and I'd then need to hope and pray that I've got enough saved in there to then carry on where I was instead of having to go back to the start and do it again. But yeah, it's going to be a long process to recover my data and I don't want to be in this situation again. So the new software that I've got, the new Synology I've got has great software. For a start, it allows me to access all of my data over the internet if I wanted to. And it's reasonably secure. The videos that I've been watching are experts on this system and they use this system. So it's reasonably secure. But you also have the ability to spend more money. This system was just over £700 just for the box, just for the enclosure. So it's a big investment that I didn't know I was going to need to make. topic: MacBook Pro check in - Gordon's Prediction for Apple Apps in the future - Writing Blogs using AI and Video
show_notes: News: EPIC Fortnite is back on iOS through Xbox Cloud Gaming Google Play is now also requiring all in-app purchases for apps in their store to go through them and not use a different payment method. This follows iOS and is what Apple's court case with EPIC is based on currently. MacBook Pro Check-in - how it's been since the purchase a few months back Speed is good, size of screen is great. Some iOS apps will now work on Apple Silicon, although not really tried. Shortcuts has come to the Mac which is really useful. It weighs more, and is a bit more bulky and deeper, but it's not a big issue. The charger doesn't always fit into coffeeshop plugs due to it's size. Gordon's Prediction - Bigger universal apps that contain the code for iOS, iPad OS, Watch OS and Mac OS - all in one app. Let's see if it happens !! Writing Blogs in a new way - using AI writing software. Theory only currently, not tried. Online AI software is a good starting point when writing blogs. I use jasper.ai which works really well (but isn't cheap) Record a video with your blog content, which for some people, including me, is quicker and easier to do. Then transcribe the video and add it to the blog under the video so that the search engines will pick up the text and index it. We have a service that transcribes videos that we have spoken about before called Happyscribe.com I am doing a talk next week on software for children's entertainers which is why I was looking into this. If you try this, then let us know in the comments how you got on.   Visit the website: https://www.thisweekwith.co.uk Drayson Design Website - https://www.draysondesign.com The Creative Tinker Website - https://www.thecreativetinker.com Facebook: https://www.thisweekwith.co.uk/facebook Youtube: https://www.thisweekwith.co.uk/youtube * Full transcript will be available on the website. [00:05:06.840] - Gordon

Yeah.

Yeah. The other thing with 80/20 is that you could get 20% of your income from 80% of your customer base, and vice versa. Which, again, is a really interesting statistic. Yeah.

Much more. So, yeah, very interesting.

From Blockbuster?

No.

Yeah.

show_notes: We rebuilt the entire website https://season-3.thisweekwith.co.uk Moved from Divi to Oxygen Reasons for the rebuild: We didn't know how long we would be doing This Week With, so didn't really plan for the future Being able to search for content was impossible The design was a pre-designed template Decided to build a custom design Looked on Pinterest and Dribbble for inspiration Mocked it up on Figma as a collaborative process Created three-page designs - home page, archive page (all episodes) and the individual page (single episode) Built with Oxygen Builder Convert all data from old site to new site: Change all episode names to new format S2E38 Changed all show notes from a list to paragraphs Converted all m4a audio episodes to mp3 format for the new site audio player Link up all the new audio files to the correct episode Changed every episode image to show the season, as well as the youtube episode thumbnail images Then went through and linked up all the new graphics everywhere Edited all youtube videos by removing the countdown timer Updated the image of Gordon everywhere, so the cut out was much better New techniques and skills learnt Now you can: Search for content, filter episodes by length, season or date using Ajax (immediate updates without reloading the page) You can then sort by Latest, Oldest, Longest and Shortest episodes Tooltips show you what an icon is for Easter eggs (hidden surprises) in the website (watch episode for full details) Compare with the old website: Home Page - All Episodes - Individual Episode Drayson Design Website - https://www.draysondesign.com The Creative Tinker Website - https://www.thecreativetinker.com Facebook: https://www.thisweekwith.co.uk/facebook Youtube: https://www.thisweekwith.co.uk/youtube

Whereas if you're loading them from a website or a kind of 'CDN' maybe, which is a 'content delivery network,' which basically is a cached version of the images, it's going to be a lot quicker to load all the images.

[00:15:23.710] - Gordon
And following on from that tip, which is great, is that if you make sure that when you specify an image within your email, you use a specific URL, it means that you can change that image any time you like. So, for example, if you've got a product image and it's got the price embedded in the image, then when you change the price of that product, all you have to do is to change the hosted image that you're sending in your emails, and automatically anybody who receives an email from that moment on will get the new image with the new price, but, this is the best bit, all of the previous people who've already received your email will see the new image. So as it's not attached to the email, it's just going to pull in the image from the Web server, every time you open that email, and if you've got a new image with a new price, new contact details, whatever it is that people who've got the email six months ago, three years ago, they're going to see the up to date information, which is huge. It means your emails are always going to show the correct information, even if they open it from the past.

[00:16:41.260] - Taylor
You just need to make sure that the the URL is the exact same. So you delete the old version and upload it, because if you upload it while the previous is there, it will normally append like one next.

[00:16:52.730] - Gordon
Correct.

[00:16:53.170] - Taylor
And that won't work, so you need to make sure you delete the old one and re-upload it with the exact same filename.

[00:16:58.390] - Gordon
So if you're doing that on WordPress, the best way to do that is to put it into your media gallery. It will then give you a URL that you can use, and there is a plug-in that you can get that allows you to replace images. And what it will do is, it will just get rid of the one that's there, put the new one up and give it the same file name. And that's the best way of doing it. I have another one.

[00:17:20.500] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:17:21.460] - Gordon
If you have a video that you want people to see in your email, do not include the video as an attachment. That's the worst thing you can do because it forces people to download the video, whether they're going to watch it or not. And the quality is going to be very low because you've got about five megabytes or so that you're guaranteed to get through on email, which is not very big. So the best way to do it is go to wherever you are hosting your video. It could be YouTube, Vimeo, anywhere like that, Wistia, and grab a screenshot of the player page. So basically the image of your video with the play button on it, use that image that's hosted on your website or somewhere on the web, use the URL of that image in your email and then your, people open the email will see the image with a play button, they will assume it's a video that they need to click on. The play button is important because that's what's going to get them to click on it. And as soon as they click on it, it will open a Web browser, it will go to the right place, and it will show your video no matter how long it is in the highest possible quality.

[00:18:36.260] - Taylor
And an advantage of that, is you can host it on your website and embed it into your website, and that means you've got them to your website and, you know, you've got, you can from there direct them, if it's a specific landing page, for example, that has a special discount or something, you've got them on your website now and you can then direct them to whatever call to action you have set in place.

[00:18:57.470] - Gordon
Yeah. Now we've moved away a little bit from how to encourage people to open your emails, but there's lots of really good best practises here. And the last one that I think I've got yeah, the last one is very similar to what you were just saying, is if you are linking to content, so, for example, you've got a price list and you have a PDF. Again, don't include it in the email because it's going to be dated. Have a link that goes to a page on your website or even to the, exactly to that PDF, although I know you don't like that version. Have a page, or the PDF, put that link in, and again, when you want to update it, just update the page, just update the PDF and then anyone who clicks on that link, even if they received the email three years ago, they will see your most up to date prices. And that goes for anything that you want to update. If, it might be an ebook, for example, have a link, get them to go to that page, and then you can always update that ebook as things change.

[00:20:06.410] - Taylor
Yes. So a bit aside from email, but along the same type of lines is one of, someone I know, Nick. He does work for a restaurant and they have a menu and it's in PDF format. And because of the current situation, it's kind of, you can't really have physical copies because of, you know everyone's gonna be touching them. So what he's decided to do is, he's created a QR code. And in that QR code, it goes to '/ourmenu.' And then all he does is he then redirects 'our menu' to that week's PDF. And every week he just redirects 'our menu' link to the new PDF. And it means he doesn't have to, he doesn't even have to have the same name for the PDF because he can change where 'our menu,' which is the base URL, gets redirected to.

[00:20:59.390] - Gordon
Yeah, that's good. There you go, a different option if you want to do that instead of replacing files, that way you can keep copies and archives.

[00:21:08.420] - Taylor
And it's a lot simpler. So if they were to share it, you can say, you know, just go to '/ebook,' or whatever. And, you know, no matter what, if they go to ebook, if you can then redirect them to the correct version or whatever, you know, it's a lot simpler and you don't have to remember a long string with like '.pdf' at the end of the URL.

[00:21:28.340] - Gordon
And last of all, your signature is really important in an email. This isn't going to help you get your emails opened, but it is going to help people who want to contact you, be able to do so. So make sure, if you've got a Facebook page, put a Facebook logo in, link it through to Facebook. Same with Twitter, Instagram, any of the social medias, YouTube. Plus your website, make sure you've got that there. And if you take phone calls, make sure your telephone number is there.

[00:21:57.020] - Taylor
And another thing is put your email address in. It may seem counterintuitive because, you know, you're sending them an email. However, if people share your your email, then they will see in the signature your email address.

[00:22:12.230] - Gordon
It may not necessarily have the header being shared with your email address in it. So that's a very good point.

[00:22:17.570] - Taylor
So if they forward it, they're not going to have your email attached to it. But if your email is in the signature, they can always find you and contact you if they need to.

[00:22:25.160] - Gordon
There you go. So, lots of tips for you, for emails. If you use any or you have any of your own tips, please leave a comment and we will share that with our viewers.

Wonderful.

I think that's it really. I spoke about animation, my new course, and I spoke about the importance of animation, which was my topic for this week.

So hopefully when he's had a chance to get to grips with the animation, we'll be able to show you some examples sometime in the future and maybe we'll come back to this.

Yeah.

And talk about how you're doing with the course.

Yeah. Wonderful.

Great. Well, thank you for joining us. As always, if you would like to follow, like and subscribe, we can be found on Facebook and YouTube. That's "This Week With," the links are on the page.

And we also have our website: thisweekwith.co.uk, which has all our past episodes that you can view with audio, video, and also the show notes.

No search facility yet, but that is something that we are planning on putting on. So keep an eye out for that. So until next week, Friday, at 1pm. We will see you then. Goodbye from me, I'm Gordon from Drayson Design.

And I'm Taylor from The Creative Tinker.

Goodbye.

Goodbye.

[00:06:59.560] - Gordon
So you're using two different systems and it's a manual process to look and see how much time "Toggle" has showing outstanding, and then...

[00:07:11.740] - Gordon
Just a list.

Ongoing list of all the different time entries.

[00:07:13.950] - Gordon
So you then have to manually find out how much time has not been billed for...

[00:07:19.600] - Taylor
Since the last time I invoice them.

[00:07:20.720] - Gordon
Put it through into the invoicing system? OK.

[00:07:24.370] - Taylor
And it's a long process with moving it over, purely because, there's two ways I could do it. I could do it, go down the just add all my previous invoices in and don't worry about the previous time tracking. However, I want to add it in so that I can then have an overview, and see how many hours have I done for this client? Which clients am I earning the most money from? [00:07:48.850] - Gordon
Yes. So the more data you've got, the more you can extrapolate from it.

[00:07:52.030] - Taylor
Yeah. The only problem is, since I started over a year ago, in July 2019, there have been over 1800 time entries.

[00:08:06.073] - Gordon
Ok. So that's a start and a stop.

[00:08:07.690] - Taylor
Yes, it probably could get condensed down, so I could do it per day, for example, which I may end up doing. I may end up doing it via, either per day or um, yeah, so...

[00:08:23.530] - Gordon
So there's no easy import system for this.

[00:08:25.150] - Taylor
No not for this, no. Which is annoying, but apart from that, everything else is kind of really, really good. [00:08:44.080] - Gordon

So recently I've been, or in the past I've had to do it manually, where every time I have to go in and duplicate it and...

[00:10:03.280] - Gordon
That's not a great system then. And that's, that was in Wave was it?

[00:10:07.180] - Taylor
I mean, Wave was great for what it was, but because I do time tracking, I needed, I wanted to be able to have it all in one place. If you don't need to time track then I would highly recommend Wave because it is free, and this new system isn't free. But...

So what's it costing you at the moment?

Yeah.

OK.

And I then was in a bit of a difficult situation because I couldn't delete them, there was no bulk delete or anything, and I had to kind of talk to the chat and the team behind it and see if they can help. [00:12:11.480] - Gordon
Especially for something that's twice the price of the one you're on now. It just wasn't at all for you.

There was a few limiting things that although they could fix it, they said that they could delete the CSVs, by the time that they got round to replying to that and stuff, I needed to move it over into a system already. And...

[00:13:05.720] - Gordon
Yep.

You know, I needed those features and functionality...

[00:13:24.050] - Taylor
So tell me more about the video with the nuns on Final Cut Pro.

[00:13:29.490] - Gordon
So the big feature that I really, really like with Final Cut Pro, which is a Mac video editor. It's made by Apple, which is the same people who make the Mac. And it's just great. I mean, when it came out, it was a standard editor and then they changed completely. So they bought a brand new version out, which was written from scratch. And it had a completely different way of working. And in the past, there was a lot of people who complained that it didn't do what they wanted it to do because they were used to the previous way of doing it. As it turns out, most of those people, if not all of those people, now agree that the new system is actually much better. But you need to get your head around it. And I was with Final Cut for the early version and then moved across to the new version and sort of got it quite quickly, so I was able to carry on working. But the one feature I really, really like is called 'MultiCam.' Any ideas what MultiCam does?

[00:14:42.020] - Taylor
It's multiple cameras.

[00:14:43.670] - Taylor
It's exactly right. So it takes two or more cameras. In this case I had two, and it will synchronise the clips from both cameras using the sound, the audio. So what you end up with is one track with two layers. OK? And then it makes it really easy to edit, because all you do is, you drag this track into your timeline and it shows whichever track you currently have selected and you can specify the video and the audio separately. So what I've done on this occasion is I had two cameras, two microphones, and they were both recording audio. So I've duped them up, I've turned on the audio for both. So you're getting the sound coming from both cameras at the same time merged together, which gives a better sound in, of everything that's going on. So there's one that's sort of in the congregation area and one that's up by the bishop. So you get good sound all the way round. And then I cut between the visuals, so between the camera video. And it's such a simple way of doing it. You press 'play,' you let it play, you've got both of the visuals showing at the same time in sync, synchronised, and you use just the number one and the number two on the keypad, and every time you press it, it makes a cut for you. And when you stop all the cuts that you made at the time you made them are done and it makes life so much easier and you can go back and tweak them if you need to. If you go, "do you know what? I want that cut sort of six frames before the cut is actually there," you can just drag it back six frames and it's perfect, and it makes life really easy. And it's one of the reasons I like doing two camera shoots because can you imagine if MultiCam feature didn't exist?

[00:16:45.810] - Taylor
It would take a lot of trying to line up.

[00:16:48.690] - Gordon
Yeah. Every single time you want to cut to a different camera, you'd have to grab the feed and try and find out the exact point that you're at, it would just be horrid. It's a really, really good system, and it's been designed to work in the same way; so it's a bit like in a live studio if you've ever seen the control room where they have lots of screens with all the different camera angles, and the director will say, "camera three, camera seven," and then the editor will live edit and go to those cameras. And it's a great system. It just makes life so much quicker and easier. So if you are looking to edit video and you've got a Mac start with "iMovie," that's a good place to start. And then if you find you need something a bit more professional, a bit more customisable, go and get Final Cut Pro. It's one off charge, not like Adobe, where they charge you every month. It's a one off cost.

[00:17:48.160] - Taylor
Wonderful. I think that's it from us this week.

[00:17:50.230] - Gordon
I think it is. So, as always, you can find us, like and subscribe on YouTube and on Facebook.

And you can also find us at thisweekwith.co.uk, where you have all the past audio, video and also our show notes.

Goodbye.

Bye bye.
