And for those of you who may want to look into BNI as a networking, one of the things that is quite interesting with the way BNI works, is that you have to commit if you become a member, you have to commit to go to BNI meetings every single week. You can't wake up in the morning and go, "oh, do you know what? I just don't fancy it today." You have to go. And if for whatever reason you're unable to go...

[00:10:59.160] - Taylor
You have to find a sub. So you can basically, you put out a request in, well for us we put a request in our region, and say, "I'm looking for a sub." And then someone from one of the other chapters can then, if they're not locked out, of course, can say, "yes, I'd like to attend" and they will then...

[00:11:16.620] - Gordon
Or somebody who's nothing to do with BNI.

[00:11:19.260] - Taylor
Yeah. And they will attend on your behalf and they will kind of stand up and give your pitch. However, they also get the opportunity to give...

[00:11:27.870] - Gordon
Their pitch, not your pitch.

[00:11:29.220] - Taylor
No, they stand up and they give my pitch.

[00:11:31.650] - Gordon
OK.

[00:11:32.130] - Taylor
Because I can't be in the room, so they're substituting for me. So they'll stand up and go, "hi, I'm Taylor from The Creative Tinker."

[00:11:37.290] - Gordon
OK.

[00:11:37.740] - Taylor
But then they also get the opportunity to have their pitch and tell people about what they're doing. So that's why it's appealing for people because you're substituting for someone, so you're not, they're not losing out on their space that they've paid for, but they also get the chance to share and what they do.

[00:11:54.180] - Gordon
Well, that's interesting because I was, I've been to many BNI meetings, but a long, long time ago, and that's very different. So let's talk about the work you do. One of the questions that you asked me last week is what I specialize in. So I'm going to ask the same back to you. What do you specialize in, as in The Creative Tinker?

[00:12:13.110] - Taylor
I mostly specialize in website design. So yours is more, I would say, more graphic design based in terms of kind of what you what most of your work entails.

[00:12:24.570] - Gordon
Yeah, mine started as website design, but I've kept a lot of the customers that I started with and they already have their website and everything done. So I've now moving on to do other work for them, which involves graphic design.

[00:12:37.950] - Taylor
So most of my work is website design, however, I can do graphic design as well, which is either normally like logos and things, or I will create stuff for websites. And I quite enjoy brochure sites or, which are kind of static sites in a way, where it kind of showcases people's services. So a lot of trades will have a 'home' page, 'about' page, a 'service' page, and then kind of 'portfolio' and 'contact.'

[00:13:04.420] - Gordon
So a website that doesn't change a great deal.

[00:13:06.600] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:13:07.680] - Gordon
Just like if you printed a brochure, you print a ton of them because you know your services aren't going to change a lot, and you're giving these out to people, you know that that's going to be the same for the length of the time that you've got those brochures.

[00:13:20.370] - Taylor
So that's quite a common website I do. I also do e-commerce sites. So I have a couple of clients who are artists, which I've done websites for, so they want to showcase and sell their work. I quite enjoy doing those. And then recently I've started taking on more complex websites. So at the moment I'm in the process of doing a job listing website for recruitment and health care professionals. And it's really interesting because I didn't have any understanding or, not understanding, I had no prior knowledge of creating...

[00:13:55.530] - Gordon
Exactly how you were going to do it.

[00:13:56.850] - Taylor
Yeah, I knew kind of the logistical, as in like, this is what I needed to do. I need to go and like look and research, I knew the areas I need to go. But I'd never actually done it. And it was really interesting, because it gave me a challenge and something to do. And then, you know, now we're in the late, last late stages of the project and it's you know, the client's come back and gone, you know, "it looks absolutely amazing, I'm loving the way it looks."

[00:14:20.520] - Gordon
And the way it works, which is more important because this is a complex website.

[00:14:24.540] - Taylor
To me that's really nice to hear, because before I had no, you know, I'd never done this before. So it was kind of a new territory for me. And the fact that they like it is, you know, and the functionality of it, is really good because...

[00:14:37.650] - Gordon
And this is great because it means that you can now take this knowledge and apply it to future jobs that come in and build upon it and become someone to go to. If you've got a really complex site, go to Taylor because he knows what he's doing, he's got the experience for it now.

[00:14:55.350] - Taylor
Yeah. And I think that even though I've got the understanding of the job listing and how to do that, it's given me the understanding to do different tasks and more advanced websites, even if they're not job listing per se, I now have a better understanding of logical, my logical skills. And also working with PHP and things like that, I have a better understanding because I needed to learn that.

[00:15:21.190] - Gordon
Which is the programming language that a lot of websites are built on, just for those who don't know what PHP stands for. So let's look to the future then. Where do you see The Creative Tinker as a company in the future? You know, let's go, so 5, 10 years time.

[00:15:39.630] - Taylor
It's a really, I've been asked this a few times. I have kind of one to one meetings with BNI members or, you know, other people. And I get asked this question. They go, "where do you see yourself? Where would you, where do you want to be?" And it's a really difficult question because, you know, obviously every business wants to grow and become bigger and earn more money. But for me, I don't want to, I don't like the idea of losing control. And so, you know, giving the creative freedom to somebody else, I think would lose the Creative Tinker 'touch,' because all the designs come from me, all my work is done by me. And so it's a real difficult because as much as I want to grow and become bigger and stuff like that, I don't want to lose control of the...

[00:16:28.380] - Gordon
Quality.

[00:16:28.830] - Taylor
The quality, yeah. Because, you know, obviously as much as you can screen in recruitment, there's still that kind of, you handing off to someone and giving them the control, and I don't like the idea of losing control. So that's been the biggest issue with me in terms of being able to grow. And it's, it will have to come down to whether or not I either get more work in, because I've been really busy. And, you know, you know, if I keep getting more work at the rate I am, I probably might need to b ring someone in because I don't have enough time.

[00:17:04.530] - Gordon
To service them all.

[00:17:04.920] - Taylor
Yeah, because I've only got a limited number of hours in a day. And even though I may be doing long hours, it's still not enough to be able to meet the services in the required time. Most projects don't have a deadline, which is nice. However, you know, you don't want to be waiting four months from when you started.

[00:17:26.830] - Gordon
No, when someone wants a website done, they want it done quickly so they can start.

[00:17:30.120] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:17:30.930] - Gordon
Getting the benefit of it.

[00:17:32.370] - Taylor
So it's trying to find that trade off and find, see if I can find someone that I'm happy that I can trust to pass work to and say, you know, "would you be able to help me?" But at the same time not losing that control.

[00:17:45.960] - Gordon
Yeah it's, it is a difficult thing. And I think if you do find the right person, the important bit is to get the process right. So the process being that you make it very clear what's required from them at every stage and have milestones where you, as soon as you hit them, there's a review and so that you can very quickly pick up on anything that might be going in the wrong direction right at the beginning before it gets too far. And I think that's a big part of growing your business. I've chosen not to grow my business personally because I do so many different things. They, they're all filling my time like entertainment, and the design side of it. I'm the only person who can actually do both of those together. So if I got someone else in and then I end up getting a magic job or a performance job, I'd need to go out and leave it with someone else, and that may not necessarily be the right thing for me to do, but it is difficult. I understand your problem there.

[00:18:57.540] - Taylor
The other issue is being able to find someone to be able to hire, especially right now is, being able to find someone that obviously I wouldn't want to hire an adult who's older than me because they're going to obviously cost more, and I probably wouldn't be able to afford...

[00:19:13.740] - Gordon
Well, only if they have the experience.

[00:19:14.970] - Taylor
Yeah, but a lot more people as you're older that have the experience will cost more. Whereas if you're trying to find someone with the same skillset that I have at my age, would be a lot harder of a task.

[00:19:28.410] - Gordon
Yes, you're right in the middle of a tricky sort of knife's edge, really, as to which way to go.

[00:19:34.260] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:19:34.800] - Gordon
So the answer is you don't really know at the moment.

[00:19:37.320] - Taylor
No.

[00:19:37.890] - Gordon
Ok, well as I'm sure you know, it's quite important to make a decision at some point soon, because if you know where you're going, the reason they ask these questions, because if you know where you're going, pretty much every question that you might ask yourself can be answered very simply by, "where are we heading? How will this help me get there?"

[00:20:00.680] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:20:01.400] - Gordon
So, yeah, I mean, maybe we'll come back to this and talk about it in a future episode and see if you've got any clearer idea of where you might be going.

[00:20:12.020] - Taylor
At the moment, I'm just enjoying building websites, you know.

[00:20:16.040] - Gordon
And making a living.

[00:20:17.090] - Taylor
I have so much passion for building websites and I just enjoy it, that if I could do it for free, I would, but obviously, because I need to make money.

[00:20:26.270] - Gordon
Don't take that as a way to come in and offer him silly money because he won't take it, he's too busy.

[00:20:32.720] - Taylor
No. But if money didn't exist, I mean, in terms of you didn't need money to survive and things like that, then I would be happy to do it because I enjoy it that much. And it's, you know, I just enjoy it.

[00:20:44.540] - Gordon
So if people have listened to this, or watched this, and thought, yeah, d'you know what, I want to get in touch and find out a bit more about what The Creative Tinker can do for them, how do they get in touch with you?

[00:20:56.870] - Taylor
You can visit my website, which is thecreativetinker.com, or you can get in touch by email or phone, which would both be on my website as well so.

[00:21:06.980] - Gordon
And the website has changed recently, but we'll get into that in a future episode.

[00:21:11.540] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:21:12.530] - Gordon
So I think that's pretty much everything we need to talk about for The Creative Tinker. Have you got anything else you want to answer?

[00:21:19.460] - Taylor
No, I think that's everything from me.

[00:21:20.930] - Gordon
So as always, thank you so much for watching. If you'd like to comment or get in contact with us about anything that we've said during this vidcast or podcast, we can be found on Facebook and YouTube, which is where we stream live at 1pm every Friday. We also have the website.

[00:21:42.380] - Taylor
Yeah, thisweekwith.co.uk.

[00:21:45.410] - Gordon
And all of our episodes are on that as well. You can get in contact with us individually on there. And I think that's it, isn't it?

[00:21:53.450] - Taylor
Yeah, I think that's everything.

[00:21:54.500] - Gordon
Thank you for joining us. My name is Gordon from Drayson Design.

[00:21:57.740] - Taylor
And I'm Taylor from The Creative Tinker.

[00:22:00.050] - Gordon
We'll see you next week. Goodbye.

[00:22:02.240] - Taylor
Bye.

transcript:
[00:00:48.580] - Gordon
Hello. My name's Gordon from Drayson Design.

[00:00:50.950] - Taylor
And I'm Taylor from The Creative Tinker.

[00:00:53.140] - Gordon
And welcome to "This Week With." So for those of you who've been with us in past weeks, you'll know that we talk about things that we've been doing during the week and any news items that we found. We've decided to make a slight change this week. We're going to spend one episode talking about my business and then we're going to spend an episode talking about Taylor's business. So seeing as I'm here and ready to go, we're going to start with me first, Drayson Design.

[00:01:27.130] - Taylor
So how did you start with Drayson Design then?

[00:01:29.330] - Gordon
It's a very good question Taylor, I'm glad you asked. So the the the reason Drayson Design started out was by mistake really, not by mistake, but it wasn't planned as such. I've been doing computers for a long time now, back in the days of the BBC Micro, which we had at school. And I really took to it; I thought it was a great little device and had lots of potential. And as a primary school student, I was the person that played with the computer the most and knew the most about it. And we only had the one, and we had different classrooms and the computer had to be taken from each class physically and then set up again. And because I knew the most about it, I was the one who got that job. So I started with computers back in the days of when I was at primary school, and it's just kept with me, really. And I was one of the first people to get a website. I got a website disbelieving.com, that was one of my first ever websites. And in fact, I bought the domain name and it was about two hundred and something pounds, which for a 'dot com' at the time was a reasonably good price. But for dot com now. Terrible.

[00:02:55.360] - Taylor
Yeah, they're about...

[00:02:57.970] - Gordon
About £57 at the moment.

[00:02:58.840] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:02:58.840] - Gordon
That's what I'm selling mine for. And that's for two years. This was only for a year when I purchased it. And so that was a long time ago. And so I built my own website and I incorporated into my website some pages for The Magic Circle, which I was a member of at the time, because they didn't have a website, they had nothing on the internet. And I thought it would be a good idea to get something up so that if anyone ever searched for 'The Magic Circle,' they'd find some information about us. So I did a few pages, and The Magic Circle were very interested in knowing about this because they originally thought I was pretending to be The Magic Circle until I printed out... Printed out, can you believe it? I printed out pages to show them what was going on, and I was just saying I'm a member and this is The Magic Circle. And they were going, "oh, this is really good. Could you do a website for us?" And I thought, "yeah, I guess so." So I started doing a Magic Circle website, so I created the first ever website for The Magic Circle. And then I had a few more people say to me, "oh, you did The Magic Circle's website, you did your own, could you do a website for me?" And as it slowly got more and more popular, the internet that is, more and more people were asking me to do websites for them. And I had lots of entertainers who were doing it, mainly magicians. And so Drayson Design sort of created itself, if you like. I didn't ever sit down and go, "right, I'm going to start a business called Drayson Design." That just didn't happen. And in fact, I've never advertised. All of the work I've got has been through word of mouth or from people seeing what I've done in the past and going, "oh, can you do that for me?"

[00:04:45.270] - Taylor
That's really good.

[00:04:46.280] - Gordon
Yeah. So that's how it started, I mean it's changed a lot since then. [sound of running water] Sounds like somebody's just washing their hands. Really important when you're in lockdown; wash your hands. There we go. Just, the taps make a terrible sound here, do apologise about that. So that's how I started. And in fact, one other thing I did when I started was, I started making databases, because as I was using a lot of, as I was doing work for a lot of entertainers, I created my own database, which ran my business basically. So, it's a database that will take bookings, allow me to send confirmations out and basically just runs the whole thing for me. And I got entertainers saying, "how do you manage your bookings? Can you do that for us?" And I was like, "yeah, yeah, I can do that. Not a problem." So I was creating custom built databases for people, which took forever. I mean, I kid you not, they took maybe a week's worth of work working full time on it, and I just I didn't get the return on the investment really for that. I didn't get enough money. I couldn't charge a week's worth of work for that because people would never have paid it. So I only did a few of those, but that, they were hard work. And in fact my database is still going and going very strong and in fact has been upgraded a bit thanks to the automation that we've been doing recently.

[00:06:25.610] - Taylor
That's really good.

[00:06:26.440] - Gordon
Hmm.

[00:06:27.480] - Taylor
So what do you specialize in? What would you say your biggest things that you do?

[00:06:32.720] - Gordon
So I do a lot of work for entertainers and entertainment. So I do lots of photography and videography for shows, whether that be promotional videos for entertainers who want to get a promo together or if it's actual performance; either a stage show or a close-up show or cabaret, that sort of thing. So I do a lot of those. Photography as well, so live event photography, we've spoken about that last week. I have also recently been asked to do posters, so promotional posters for shows. And in fact, there's two companies that I work for and do all of their posters and publicity. So they have adverts on TVs in the venue; and they have big banners they put outside the venue; and they have some newsletters and things. So I do the posters; I do all the banners; all the flyers; all the online advertising for them; all the artwork for any print that they do. And so I do that for two companies at the moment and they have several productions a year, so that keeps me quite busy creating a look for them and a style for them for that particular show. And in fact, the last one I did for one of the companies, I did the photography for as well. So I actually went to the theatre, we took some photographs of the actual cast members and they got to be put directly onto the poster. Which is a lot more work, but I think it works really well because, just like all the big pantomimes, for example, they have all the the cast members, the famous people, on the poster, and that's what brings people in. And even though these shows are amateur shows, you still find that there are people who will go and support these and they have people they like to watch in these shows. And if they see those people on the posters, they'll go, "oh, I'll go and watch this, because that person I like is in it." So that seems to be working quite well, although we do need to sort of work out some pricing on this because it's a lot more work when I take the photos for it as well. So something else I specialize in is websites for entertainers, which I mentioned earlier. And trying to get the right feel, and look, and style for a website that suits that entertainer is something that I enjoy doing. And it's something that is important because otherwise all websites for all entertainers will look the same. And that's no good. There was a while back when there was a fashion of every entertainer, children's entertainer in particular, having a cartoon image of themselves done, with some sort of circle around them and maybe a puppet in there. And pretty much everybody that I know who's a children's entertainer had one of these done. Not me, I might add. I didn't because everyone else was doing it. So because everyone was doing it, I wanted to be different and make sure I didn't have that. So I have a completely different look and branding. But for a while, lots of people were doing this. And so all the websites that were coming out, even though they were done by lots of different people, they all looked very similar because they all had this logo, this mark, which was in the same style because the person they all went to was the same person, and he had a certain style when he when he illustrates. So finding a way to build a website that looks different when you've got very similar graphics is also quite difficult to do. But you also have to take a lead from the actual entertainer and what they do; their personality; how they wish to come across; any branding that they currently already have; that sort of thing has to be taken into account. And so, yeah, that's one of the things I specialize in. And more recently, I have been creating and collecting and making my own tools. So services, it's called 'Software As A Service,' SAAS, where you pay a yearly or a monthly fee and you have access to a service that does something for you. So for example, Online Booking Assistant, that's one of my services, and that is a yearly cost. And then we've got the more recent things like the reviews and the testimonials. And there's another new service that I've got that will be coming online soon, which I'll talk about in a future episode. So, yes, re-selling those as well. That's pretty much the bulk of my work for Drayson Design, I guess. But then I get, you know, one offs that come along doing specific documentary; or doing a specific graphic design for something; or creating or laying out a book so that that can go off to the printer; that sort of thing.

[00:11:57.400] - Taylor
That's quite nice as well, because it means that it splits up your regular work and it gives you something different to try or learn and it gives you something to learn if you haven't done it before. I know especially, I quite like trying new projects and things that I have never done before. You know, when sometimes clients come to me going, "can you do this?" And I think, you know, I have an idea of how to do it and stuff, and I kind of learn as I go. And that helps me in the future, because if then someone comes to me again, I already have a good understanding, so it's.

[00:12:26.980] - Gordon
Yeah. I mean, I would never take money from someone whom I didn't think I would be able to do a good job for. So I would have to, in the back of my head, I would have to know that I'm capable of doing it, even if it's something I haven't necessarily got experience with in the particular way they want it. I must have experience in other ways so that I know that I'm going to be able to fulfil the contract.

[00:12:51.700] - Taylor
So normally what happens is people will come to me and go, "can you do this?" And I know, like in my head, I know the logic and stuff but, and I've seen other people use it, and I've, I'm in like a bunch of forums and stuff, so I see people talking about it and stuff like that, so I know it's possible...

[00:13:05.270] - Gordon
And we know that we've got other people we know who are experts in their field that should we run into problems, we can go to them and say, "right, look, I've got a little job for you. Can you help me with this? Can you do this?"

[00:13:16.660] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:13:16.900] - Gordon
"Can I just pass this bit over to you? Because you can do it quicker than me." We've built up a good, what's the? Community of professionals who have their own expertise we can call on as and when we need to, which is always good.

[00:13:32.630] - Taylor
Yeah, definitely. So how have things changed since you started Drayson Design to now I guess.

[00:13:40.660] - Gordon
So, it's changed a lot. As I said, I was one of the first people to ever get a website. And in fact, I've got some very early business cards which we'll display on the screen now for you.

[00:13:54.430] - Taylor
If you can find them.

[00:13:55.510] - Gordon
No, we've got them. All lined up. Yeah! Live show. You've got to have them ready. There you go. So, you can see them now. And yeah, so they look very different. If I show you my recent business card here... You can see that it's changed a lot. Yeah. It's just, the very fact that the internet itself has just boomed. The people that you would never think would have internet access, like grandparents, for example, new technology, that sort of thing, why would they need that? But they do. I know pretty much, everyone I know, pretty much everyone I know, has internet. My uncle doesn't, but he's chosen not to, that's basically his choice. But everyone else I know has got internet, and that wasn't the case before. When I started out, I was the only person I knew with internet. And it wasn't even broadband. It was a modem, you used to... Originally it was a phone coupler. You used to dial the number on a rotary phone, ok, way before your time. Once you hear the tone, you put it in an audio coupler. If you've seen the film "War Games," you'll know what I'm talking about. And that would then take the sounds and convert them into, take them down a signal into the computer and convert, the computer would then convert those sounds into data. And that's how it was. And when I started out, I was on a bulletin board system, which meant you dialled in... It, the computer then sent your messages; received new messages; logged you off. You would then read those messages; you'd reply to them, offline; you would then log on again and you would send your new messages; download any new messages. And it meant that no one else could use the phone because if they picked it up at the time that you were sending and receiving messages, they'd hear this horrible sound. I mean, it's just, if you've ever heard it, you'll know what I mean. And the number of times that my parents would just pick up the phone because they needed to make a call and they'd hear me and they'd shout, "Gordon, get off the phone, we need to make a call." It's like, "yeah, well, I'm off now because you've just hung up my connection." But I mean, the connections were never long. They were sort of, you know, two, three minutes at a time, but they were, short periods, but they were, they happened a lot. You know, they would happen three, four times a night if I was, you know, talking to people. And then we got given an email address. It's like, wow, we got an email address. Why do I need that? I didn't, I couldn't understand why I needed it, because at the time it was just a small community and you used to log in and everyone was on the one bulletin board system and that was it. You talk to the people who were on the system that you'd chosen to subscribe to. And it was a subscription, you had to pay money to be on there. And then they came and they said your email address can now be used to communicate with other bulletin board systems around the world. It was like ok that's, so hang on, I can send a message here and my friend who's interested in computers in Canada, he can pick up that message and send it back to me, and it's not a phone call, it's an actual, a message? I thought, "right, ok, I'm starting to understand how this email could be interesting." And then websites came along. So, yeah, it's really interesting how it's changed. I mean, a picture, to just download a picture used to take seven minutes. Seven minutes to download a very low res picture in today's terms, and now I'm recording video, you know, on phones and on mobile devices, you know, they're just, and they're instantly going onto computers. It's just very, very different. And as a designer for websites and photography and videography, all of those have changed so much in the time that I've been doing it. Learning how to do something, you had to get your hands dirty, you had to just get a book from the library, buy a book, learn how to do something, teach yourself HTML. And it then send them an email with all their details, so it pulls in their name, price, the type of product it is; and then has a button which they can click, which when they click on it, it will open up a new email. It automatically pre-fills the send email to my renewals email, adds, it says, "Hi Taylor, please renew" and then puts the service in, it puts their company name in, and it says "thank you. From" and then puts their name in. All they need to do is click 'send.' That comes straight to me. I can then update the spreadsheet and say "yes, they want to renew." This will then stop sending the emails, the renewal emails for the...

[00:12:13.420] - Gordon
Because they've already renewed.

[00:12:15.010] - Taylor
They've said they want to renew.

[00:12:16.080] - Gordon
Yeah.

[00:12:16.360] - Taylor
And so it'll stop sending the reminder 14 day and on the day...

[00:12:19.510] - Gordon
Yep.

[00:12:19.780] - Taylor
Email. I will then send them a invoice manually. Once they have paid I click, tick for 'paid.'

[00:12:27.160] - Gordon
Yep.

[00:12:28.030] - Taylor
This then will send them a thank you email saying, "thank you for renewing."

[00:12:31.780] - Gordon
Yep.

[00:12:31.780] - Taylor
And it wipes all of the ticks basically that I have set so that it's back fresh and updates their renewal by one year.

[00:12:40.870] - Gordon
Very good. So it basically automates all of the renewals and lets the customers pay you, or let you know you want to renew... Let you know that they want to renew, at which point you renew; send them an invoice; once it's paid it puts them on the bottom of the list again and waits until their renewal date comes around.

[00:12:59.170] - Taylor
Pretty much.

[00:12:59.950] - Gordon
Yeah. So if you have a similar sort of system or you're looking to get a similar sort of system, then you need to contact Taylor, details will be at the end. And he can create a system for you that will do exactly what his system does and basically create a bit of automation in your business.

[00:13:17.870] - Taylor
It can be really good for saving time if you, I know a lot of tradespeople, they're admin is always not the best because they're always out working, doing jobs, and they don't have the time to normally sit down. I mean, they probably do at the moment. But don't normally have the time to sit down and, you know, sort their admin out fully, working. And so having something automated can be really helpful and beneficial because it's one less thing you need to worry about. And yeah it just...

[00:13:44.010] - Gordon
And he's doing all of this while still trying to be able to see through his hair, due to the fact he can't go and get a haircut.

[00:13:51.150] - Taylor
Yeah. I could do it, I need the back and sides need doing.

[00:13:55.120] - Gordon
Yeah. And some of the fringe. Anyway, I think that's pretty much it for today. Seems like our conversation today was all about automation and bad internet, which don't go hand in hand at all, but anyway. So please, if you are watching this on Facebook, please leave a comment and let us know that you were here. Let us know what you thought of it. If there's any questions you have, let us know, we'll try and answer those. We're also streaming live on YouTube now. Now, we don't have an address yet because you have to have a 100 subscribers before you can get your own vanity URL, or vanity address, so we don't have that yet so the link will be on the page now. So go and join us. If you hit the 'subscribe' button and then the little 'bell' icon that will notify you when we go live next. That's it from me. Thank you so much for joining us. My name's Gordon. You can find me at draysondesign.com.

[00:14:57.420] - Taylor
And I'm Taylor and you can find me at thecreativetinker.com.

[00:15:02.250] - Gordon
So thanks for joining us and we'll see you next week with "This Week With."

[00:15:07.920] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:15:09.020] - Gordon
Bye bye.

[00:15:09.850] - Taylor
Take care. Bye.

transcript:
[00:00:00.420] - Gordon
Maybe some software that we're using or some ideas.

[00:00:04.290] - Taylor
Benefit from things that we've learnt while, you know, being self-employed or, you know, what we do in our day to day lives to make things easier and better so, yeah.

[00:00:15.450] - Gordon
So let us tell you a little bit about ourselves. My name is Gordon and I run a company called "Drayson Design." And both of our companies are very similar. I do hosting of websites, building of websites and print design. I also do videography and photography as well. Taylor?

[00:00:35.970] - Taylor
I'm mostly just web design, so building websites, developing things for, custom coding things and I also host websites as well.

[00:00:47.370] - Gordon
And your company name?

[00:00:48.570] - Taylor
"The Creative Tinker" is...

[00:00:50.280] - Gordon
"The Creative Tinker." So you can find me on Drayson Design. I'm on social media, and the same with Taylor; The Creative Tinker. So Taylor, let's start with you. What have you been up to this week?

[00:01:03.450] - Taylor
So this week I've been working on a few projects that have come in. First one is a health care website. So what they are is, they're like a recruiting agency for health care staff. So people that want to find part time jobs, full time jobs, anything to do in the health care sector, really. I think it's both public and private sector, I believe.

[00:01:24.810] - Gordon
And that's really important at the moment because we're recording this in lockdown. So coronavirus is all over the place and we are on week 4 now, I think, of being in lockdown. So building a website for health professionals is quite topical, really, isn't it?

[00:01:41.520] - Taylor
Yeah. And we've got to try and get it done as quickly as possible because obviously it's quite urgent and in need so that's one of the websites I've been working on. And another one is for a building company. They are re-, its a redesign of their website. So they want to bring it up to date and more modern. Their website was built quite a while ago by themselves, and they just want to update it with all their new projects that they've done and, you know, really showcase off what they can offer and show their potential clients, I guess, what they what they can bring and yeah just really modernize it and bring it to become better, really.

[00:02:20.610] - Gordon
And have you come across any problems that you've had to problem solve on either of these websites this week?

[00:02:27.630] - Taylor
Not yet. I mean, one of them is trying to install and put together the users so people can register and log in and kind of sort that and make sure that works properly. So that's the only real problem with the health care website.

[00:02:42.870] - Gordon
Yes, so building a sort of a membership side to a website is always difficult because there's so many different ways you can do it and different functionality that you can have. It could be that you just want people to be able to log in just so that they can access pages or files that, you know, the normal visitor can't access. But that's not quite what you are needing to do with your health care site, is it?

[00:03:09.090] - Taylor
So they'll need to be able to apply for jobs and things like that. Also, look at their current jobs that they've applied for in their own profile section, upload their CV so that it's already in there so they can just one click and kind of apply without having to put their details in every time. Yeah, and making sure that the, both recruiters and the employers, and the kind of employees or the prospects, both get emails to say you were accepted, you weren't accepted, you've got a new offer, etc, etc. So it was kind of trying to get that to work with each other, really.

[00:03:46.020] - Gordon
And one of the things that we're using to do our processing of forms is a piece of software called "Fluent Forms." There's a lot of ways that you can do this. Now, both Taylor and I use WordPress as our basis for all the websites that we build, mainly because it's user friendly and not from a developer point of view, but from a user's point of view or an owners point of view.

[00:04:13.200] - Taylor
Yep.

[00:04:13.200] - Gordon
So the owner of a website doesn't actually have to know too much to be able to manage their own website.

[00:04:18.990] - Taylor
It's a great framework as well for, especially for local and small businesses that don't have the capital or the money to invest, you know, three, four, five thousand pounds plus into a website, because you've already got that framework built in that you can kind of get yourself started with.

[00:04:36.090] - Gordon
And there's always more 'plug-ins,' as they call them, which add functionality to an existing website when new technology comes along. So, for example, when Instagram came along, you know, WordPress had been out for a long time before Instagram, but there was a plug-in available that you could just bring in your Instagram pictures straight to your website.

[00:04:56.520] - Taylor
Yeah, just embedding them straight in and, you know, it's more user friendly rather than developer friendly. I mean, there's lots of developer functionality that you can, you really dive into the actual PHP code and all of that, but from a user point of view, it's kind of click and play from their side, if they want to just install something onto it you can just do that.

[00:05:17.520] - Gordon
Yeah, it's a little bit like Microsoft Word or Google Docs, you know, you can use an editor to create new pages, to create new blog posts, that sort of thing. But getting back to Fluent Forms, there are lots of different ways to have a form on your website, but just filling in the form is only the first part of it. What are you then going to do with that data? So with your website that you're doing for the health professionals, your data is going to be very specific information that has to go to a specific place, to be able to then be used in a specific way.

[00:05:53.520] - Taylor
Yes.

[00:05:54.660] - Gordon
And Fluent Forms is a really good way of doing that. We are, we haven't used it for long actually, but so far it's been really good. And in fact, they've just brought out brand new functionality, which allows you to integrate payment providers so you can add Stripe or PayPal to a form. So if you need people to pay for something, you can now do that. And that's only just come out, hasn't it?

[00:06:18.660] - Taylor
Yeah, they've got lots of other integrations, so they integrate with a lot of kind of email marketing companies, so you've got 'MailChimp,' 'Active Campaigns,' 'Moosend,' all of that lot as well as other CRMs, so I think they...

[00:06:35.340] - Gordon
CRM being a Customer Relationship Manager, just for those who aren't sure. It basically keeps all your customers' details together in one place and then as people fill in forms and so on, it will add their information to their records so you can always see everything about that one customer.

[00:06:53.010] - Taylor
Yes, so it kind of, it allows you to find out where they are maybe in a process. So if you are trying to on board client, you could see, are they, have they signed up? Are they just, have they got your first email, the second email, kind of thing. But yeah, you can integrate with things like that. You've got "Infusionsoft," which is another CRM as well...

[00:07:10.410] - Gordon
Or 'Keep' as it's now called.

[00:07:11.230] - Taylor
Yeah. Also, you've got...

[00:07:12.720] - Gordon
It's difficult when you, when you're used to a software having a name for so long. We've known it as Infusionsoft for years. And now they're gone and changed it to Keep. So we keep having to remind ourselves it's got a new name.

[00:07:24.510] - Taylor
As well as things like Google Sheets as well, which means you can manipulate the data and use formulas and things, which I think's quite interesting and pretty cool.

[00:07:33.660] - Gordon
So one of the things I've been working on this week is, I, because I also run another company, which is a magician company. So I'm a magician. I do children's shows; I do shows for big groups; I do close up; I do cabaret; I've got a double act. So I've got lots of different shows that I do. And because I'm in lockdown, I can't do any shows. There's no one having parties; there's no one celebrating anything; there's no one having corporate launches. So I am sitting at home not able to do my shows. So I came up with the idea of doing a "MagiCall," see what I did there? Magical.

[00:08:14.100] - Taylor
Very clever.

[00:08:14.370] - Gordon
Yeah, I thought so. It's like C-A-double L at the end. So it's a Magic Call. So it's a Zoom call and I'm limiting it to children's birthdays because of all the people that are affected by the lockdown I think children are pretty much the ones that are having the most hard time understanding what's going on.

[00:08:33.680] - Taylor
Struggling, why.

[00:08:34.710] - Gordon
Yeah, they're not going to school, they're being schooled at home, which is really strange for them. And if you've got your birthday, it's so difficult to explain to a five year old why they're not allowed to have all their friends to come over and and grandma and all the family to celebrate this birthday. And it's, you know, they're stuck with just the people in the house.

[00:08:55.260] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:08:55.260] - Gordon
So what I came up with was a 10 minute 'MagiCall.' So basically just using Zoom, as everyone is at the moment.

[00:09:02.430] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:09:03.150] - Gordon
So people will book in a call, and that will be for the day of the birthday party and for about 10 minutes or so I'll do some magic for them over the camera. And one of the ways that I've been trying to work out how to manage it all is to have people fill in a form to book in a session, and the form will give me all the information I need, plus a bit of extra information. And then the idea is all that information will go into a Google spreadsheet automatically. And then I can take that information, grab the bits I need to create a Zoom scheduled call; so it goes into Zoom and it all scheduled so that it knows when I'm going to do it. I can then send that information through to the customer, so they've got the login details for the Zoom call at the time that it needs to be available to them, as well as giving them a couple of other things they need to do, one of which is to let me know that they've got Zoom and that they've downloaded a PDF and printed it. And my whole system is geared to do that now and it's quite a complex system, but it actually is really easy to now run. So it took a bit of time to set up, but it's needing to run. And the problem I'm having at the moment is that Fluent Forms has a Google Sheets integration, which means that it will send everything to Google Sheets except it's a bit flaky at the moment, it's not working. So I've spoken to their support who are very good. They bring out updates and fixes.

[00:10:34.160] - Taylor
They have a roadmap as well which...

[00:10:35.280] - Gordon
They have a roadmap. Yeah. They bring them out really quickly, though. They're quite good at implementing things. And I've been speaking to support for probably about a week or so now, and other people are now having this problem. So it's not isolated to me, which means as far as they're concerned, it's not my fault. So they've decided that if other people are having a problem, it's something that they need to fix so it's become a top priority for them. So hopefully that will be back up and running very, very soon.

[00:11:06.020] - Taylor
Yeah, that's good.

[00:11:07.460] - Gordon
So something else I've been working on is, because I'm in lockdown, my company website. It's funny because I'm always working on other people's websites you never get time to do your own.

[00:11:23.240] - Taylor
A web designer's website is always the worst, because it never gets updated.

[00:11:27.960] - Gordon
It never gets updated. It's using very old technology normally. It's like a plumber's taps they say. A plumber is always out fixing everyone else's taps and plumbing issues and they've always got leaky taps at home because they never have the time to get round to doing their own. And it's been a bit like that for me. Drayson Design's website I feel really, really bad in telling you, is about 10 years old. So I've actually taken it offline. So if you were to go to draysondesign.com, you will see there's a holding page, depending on when you're watching this. If you're watching it now there'll be a holding page, hopefully...

[00:12:05.440] - Taylor
Or listening.

[00:12:06.350] - Gordon
Or listening, yes, that's right. And hopefully if you're listening to it sort of and coronavirus is but a past memory, there should be a nice shiny brand new website up and running perfectly because that's what I'm working on at the moment. And it's really difficult finding a style that I like that shows what I do. Because I've been doing this now since 1998. So this is the 22nd year for me doing this, which is quite a long time in internet. It's, you know, the internet is...

[00:12:41.360] - Taylor
Brand new when you did it.

[00:12:41.570] - Gordon
It's what?

[00:12:41.930] - Taylor
It was brand new when you.

[00:12:42.650] - Gordon
Yeah it was, it was. I mean websites were very rare when I started and everyone's got a website nowadays, hence the reason for setting up Drayson Design. But yeah, it's difficult to find the style and sit down. I've been struggling with that a bit. So hopefully, in a little while, you'll be able to go to draysondesign.com and you'll see this shiny brand new website and it'll be all working wonderfully.

[00:13:08.600] - Taylor
Wonderful. Yeah. Sounds good.

[00:13:09.890] - Gordon
So Taylor had a different point of view with this because he's not been running long, about a year or so.

[00:13:15.890] - Taylor
I started in July 2019.

[00:13:18.320] - Gordon
Ok. So we're coming up to a year for The Creative Tinker.

[00:13:21.350] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:13:21.740] - Gordon
But he didn't have any customers when he started so his first job was to create the brand and the website. So he's sort of come at it from the point of view that I came at it 22 years ago. We have no customers build, our own website.

[00:13:38.360] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:13:39.290] - Gordon
So his website is actually really good. So if you get a chance to look at it. How do they find it?

[00:13:43.880] - Taylor
Go to thecreativetinker.com. That's thecreativetinker.com. Yeah.

[00:13:50.030] - Gordon
So anything else you want to add to this?

[00:13:52.370] - Taylor
I don't think so, I think, you know, we've covered what who we are, what we're going to be doing and talking about, we explained a bit about the kind of software we've used this week.

[00:14:02.010] - Gordon
Yeah.

[00:14:02.510] - Taylor
And what we've been working on really. I mean, it's not just, you know, dedicated to just what we've been doing that week. You know, might have product showcases or software showcases for one week.

[00:14:13.160] - Gordon
Yeah.

[00:14:13.610] - Taylor
Where we talk about one piece of software.

[00:14:16.340] - Gordon
Maybe something that solved a problem that we are looking, that we've recently solved, or maybe software that we've just come across and we think, "oh, that's going to be useful in the future." So I think that's about it for this week.

[00:14:45.440] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:14:46.280] - Gordon
So thank you very much for joining us. This is all very new to us. We've not done this before, so we're still building it, we're still putting it together, finding a style. So currently you can find us on YouTube and Facebook.

|I thought we were going for Vimeo?

[00:15:02.810] - Gordon
Yeah, the video will be on Vimeo, but we'll be promoting it, live streaming this on Facebook and on YouTube. So find us there. Don't know what the names are at the moment. Probably we'll put it on screen somewhere here.

[00:15:16.490] - Taylor
Yeah.

[00:15:16.910] - Gordon
So you should be able to see it.

[00:15:18.530] - Taylor
Hopefully have a website as well that we can build and...

[00:15:21.290] - Gordon
Yeah, if we get enough people watching and it becomes sort of something that you think is of interest, then let us know and we'll do more of these and then we can, we can build a website and people can follow us and hopefully you'll get something out of this. So let us know if there's anything in particular you want to ask us, any questions. And yeah, we'll see how we go.

[00:15:45.980] - Taylor
I've been Taylor from The Creative Tinker.

[00:15:48.320] - Gordon
And I've been Gordon from Drayson Design. We'll see you next week. Bye.

Take care.
